findings.title: Preserve the light-theme contrast of expanded-post attribution links
findings.body: The light-theme branch changes the expanded-post attribution link from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 70%, rather than preserving the existing value. With a #333 primary on a white background, this changes approximately #707070 to #c2c2c2, reducing contrast from about 5:1 to 1.8:1. These small attribution links become difficult to read in light themes. Keep the light branch at 30% and use the complementary 70% secondary scaling for the dark branch.

findings.title: Keep group-member names at their existing light-theme lightness
findings.body: The group-member name previously used 30% primary lightness, but the new light-theme branch uses 50%. The same change occurs in mobile/user.scss at line 497. For a #333 primary on white, this changes the name from approximately #707070 to #999999, dropping contrast from about 5:1 to 2.8:1 and removing its contrast distinction from the member title. Preserve the original 30% light-theme branch and use 70% secondary scaling for dark themes in both files.

findings.title: Adjust the badge foreground when making its dark-theme background dark
findings.body: The default notification badge now uses a dark background in dark themes, but its foreground remains $secondary, including the explicit &[href] rule. For a dark palette with black secondary, the new background is approximately #4d4d4d while the count text is black, giving only about 2.5:1 contrast for 11px text. Previously the primary-based background was light and the secondary foreground remained readable. Change the dark-theme foreground to a contrasting color, or retain a sufficiently light background; otherwise default badge counts become difficult to read.
